basis: Congenital cardiac defects and acral skeletal malformations define this dysplasia; evidence is insufficient for additional axes across both subtypes.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in the skin and hair follicle sheath.
Parasitic infection predominantly infiltrating liver; hepatic cysts in 80-99%. Extrahepatic lesions are under 30%; reactive blood-count changes do not establish direct blood injury.
Permanent digital contractures and abnormal taurine/amino-acid excretion define the syndrome. Aminoaciduria alone does not establish kidney damage.
Intellectual disability and developmental impairment define the disorder; strabismus in 4/4 and hyperopic astigmatism in 30-79% support ocular involvement.
The defining abnormalities affect the cornea and hip joint.
Neurodevelopmental disease with frequent limb malformations supporting skeletal involvement (about 30% or more). Redistribution lymphopenia alone does not establish immunodeficiency.
Inherited epidermal fragility and blistering; palmoplantar blistering reported in 18/18.
Eyelid absence, macrostomia and skin dysplasia define syndrome; developmental delay ~67%. Common ear/hearing and skeletal abnormalities omitted at four-axis cap.
Glycosylation disorder defined by neurodevelopmental and ocular disease; coagulopathy occurs in 30-79%. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic dysfunction.
Inflammation of the abdominal peritoneum; the umbrella includes infectious and noninfectious causes, so an infectious mechanism is not universal.
Inherited retinal cone degeneration causing visual dysfunction.
Adult cystic teratomas predominantly arise in gonads, outside the axes; no alternative origin is specified. Differentiated tissue contents do not determine the organ label.
Small-fiber sensory neuropathy defines disease. Fractures in 3/3 are explicitly traumatic consequences of analgesia, rather than direct skeletal damage.
Cutaneous capillary malformation with associated epidermal changes; both skin and its abnormal blood vessels define the lesion.
Congenital or hereditary deficiency of pituitary hormone function; additional organ damage is not consistent across the umbrella.
Hemolytic red-cell disease with defining microvascular occlusion. Retinopathy, CKD, osteonecrosis and gallstones are separately diagnosed complications despite frequent HPO annotations.
Inherited degeneration or dysfunction of cerebellar and corticospinal pathways; extra-neurologic findings are subtype-specific.
Congenital duplication and mirror-pattern malformation of the lower limb and foot.
Tumor originates in the tunica vaginalis surrounding the testis, a reproductive site outside the 13 axes.
Central disorder of sleep-wake regulation causing persistent hypersomnolence and prolonged sleep.
Carcinoma arising in the stomach; no common additional organ occupation is established.
Benign vascular neoplasm; the supplied ancestry establishes blood-vessel origin but does not specify a skin or other organ site.
Pulmonary fibrosis and bone marrow failure are the defining alternative manifestations; pulmonary fibrosis reported in 15/20.
Congenital motor pathway disorder producing involuntary mirror movements; no primary skeletal muscle disease is established.
